text: Then the snow came, and after the snow came the frost. The streets looked as if they were made of silver, they were so bright and glistening; long icicles like crystal daggers hung down from the eaves of the houses, everybody went about in furs, and the little boys wore scarlet caps and skated on the ice. The poor little Swallow grew colder and colder, but he would not leave the Prince, he loved him too well. He picked up crumbs outside the baker’s door when the baker was not looking and tried to keep himself warm by flapping his wings.
title: The Happy Prince — Page 16: The Frost
director_note: I staged the prince high on his column with the swallow close beside him, so the frost and silver streets read as a distant hardship below while their loyalty stays intimate. The swallow's descent to the baker's door turns his need for crumbs into the scene's central action, ending in frantic wing-flapping against the cold.
